solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rotter deserts love having accepted ring

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the ring goes inside SANDS + O

blocks.note: love = O, nil in a tennis score

explanation.surface: A cad walks out on his sweetheart once she has taken his engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: SANDS + O is built first; the ring then goes in after the opening S, so the two Os come from different words.
explanation.definitionFit: A so-and-so is a mild euphemism for an unpleasant person, just as a rotter is.

clue.text: Discharge / rifle

blocks.note: discharge as in dismissing an employee
rifle as a verb: to ransack or plunder

explanation.surface: An order to fire a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words look military, but both are verbs: dismiss someone, and plunder a place, as soldiers sack a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Two plain synonyms: one for dismissing a worker, one for plundering a captured town.

clue.text: Gunners looking up securely fix light

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means reading from bottom to top, so RA turns round

blocks.note: to clamp is to fix firmly

explanation.surface: Artillerymen glance upward while bolting down a searchlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunners' for RA is a standing convention: the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp is a light made by an electric arc between two electrodes.

clue.text: Murder good [for] execution

blocks.note: to do in is to murder

explanation.surface: A macabre ruling that a murder is fine grounds for an execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execution' is a trap next to 'Murder': it means the carrying out of a task, not a hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: execution in its sense of carrying out a task, as the doing of it.

clue.text: Unwanted legislation performs poorly

blocks.note: over = left over, surplus to needs

explanation.surface: A complaint that some laws nobody asked for are working badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performs' sounds like a law in operation; it is an actor on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who overacts hams it up, performing badly by doing too much.

clue.text: Area with tar outside local that surfaces road

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun: the stuff that surfaces a road

indicators.note: the sailor stands outside, so SALT wraps round PH

blocks.note: a tar and an old salt are both sailors
a local is a pub; PH = public house, as on British maps

explanation.surface: Tar being spread outside the neighbourhood pub to lay a new road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' sits right beside a road-surfacing answer, but here it is the sailor, a jack tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the tarry mix spread over roads.

clue.text: Ruddy-cheeked seaman drunk

explanation.surface: A red-faced sailor who has had too much.
explanation.walkthrough: AB for an able seaman is a standing convention; 'drunk' is the noun, a drinker, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablush means blushing, pink in the face.

clue.text: Venetian dotard [in] Plato anon written out

indicators.note: writing a text out afresh can reorder its letters

explanation.surface: An old Venetian fool figures in something Plato will write up shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantalone is the doddering Venetian merchant of the commedia dell'arte; English calls him Pantaloon.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantaloon is the stock foolish old man of Italian comedy, from Venice.

clue.text: Article takes shape about United[’s] clanger

indicators.note: GELS goes about, around, U

blocks.note: a plan gels when it takes shape
U = United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A newspaper report on a football club's blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clanger' is British slang for a blunder, and the football setting leans on it; here it is something that clangs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is the church bell rung for the Angelus prayer, so it clangs.

clue.text: Book time in LA clubs perhaps going up together

indicators.note: the time goes into the turned-round letters
in a down clue, going up means reading upward, so LA SUIT turns round

blocks.note: clubs are one suit in cards

explanation.surface: A note that a booking was made while card clubs in Los Angeles were rising together.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Alone is the third Gormenghast novel by Mervyn Peake. 'Book' first suggests reserving; it is a volume. 'Together' gives ONE through the phrase 'as one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the answer is a novel, the third in Mervyn Peake's Gormenghast series.

clue.text: Red [and] black rock surrounding ridge

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose on all sides, so the rock wraps round the ridge

blocks.note: a chine is a ridge, as of hills or a backbone

explanation.surface: A description of a rock face banded red and black around a ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red and black' reads as a colour pair, but 'Red' is the whole definition and 'black' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a crimson dye made from insects, so it names a red.

clue.text: Man-at-arms called out [in] sorrow

indicators.note: calling out a word says it, so only its sound counts

blocks.note: a knight is a man-at-arms; drop the silent K

explanation.surface: A soldier crying out in grief.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a figurative one: night as the darkness of grief, as in a dark night of the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Night stands for a time of gloom or sorrow in poetic use.

clue.text: Disguised as a blue agent circling second Labour venue

indicators.note: a disguise rearranges appearances, so the letters are jumbled
the jumbled letters circle the S

explanation.surface: A spy dressed as a Tory infiltrating a Labour Party meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics blue is the Conservative colour and Labour a party, but this labour is one of the twelve of Hercules.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning the Augean stables was the fifth labour of Hercules, so the stables were a labour's venue.

clue.text: Booking sensational comedian

blocks.note: a card is a joker, a comic person

explanation.surface: A theatre agent hiring a comic who is a sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booking' reads as an engagement for a comedian; in football a player shown the yellow card is said to be booked.
explanation.definitionFit: A booking in football is a caution, shown with a yellow card.

clue.text: Speed up current softly ebbing in river

indicators.note: an ebbing tide flows back, so TIDE + P turns round
the turned letters go in the river

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: A boatman urged to hurry as the stream quietly falls away on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ebbing' fits the tidal surface so well that it hides its job as the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from the Latin for freeing the feet: to hasten a process.

clue.text: Girl made grand [in] con over not much

blocks.note: to do someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: A woman who made a thousand pounds from a small swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' tempts as a thousand pounds; the girl is Eliza Doolittle of Pygmalion and My Fair Lady, the flower seller trained to pass as a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza Doolittle is the girl Professor Higgins turns into a grand lady.

clue.text: Persons inside university before Liberal official

indicators.note: CONS comes before U and L

blocks.note: cons are convicts, people inside prison

explanation.surface: A list of students enrolled at a university ahead of a Liberal official's visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persons inside university' reads as students; 'inside' belongs with 'Persons' and means in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is a state official posted abroad, or one of Rome's chief magistrates.

clue.text: Source for certain bars in a very unusual key

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal order

explanation.surface: A musician's source for some bars of music written in an odd key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' and 'key' make a musical score; the bars are wine bars, which a vineyard supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: A vineyard is the source of wine, and so of what wine bars sell.

clue.text: Mission disheartened military force

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the middle letters, AT

blocks.note: a legation is a diplomatic mission; its heart AT goes

explanation.surface: A dispirited army on a failing campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mission' reads as a military operation; it is a diplomatic legation.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion is a body of soldiers, as in the Roman legions or the Foreign Legion.

clue.text: Travel north: party with the French [in] boat

explanation.surface: Plans for a party heading north with French guests, by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Four small conventional pieces in a row; 'the French' for LA is the standard way to get a French article.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is the flat-bottomed boat of the Venice canals.

clue.text: Offence outside hotel following MDMA party

indicators.note: SIN goes outside the rest
F is the abbreviation for following

blocks.note: f. = following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A drugs offence outside a hotel after an ecstasy-fuelled party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' ends the clue as a rave; it is the Irish political party. The offence splits in two around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinn Féin is an Irish republican political party.

clue.text: Some evidence lover dropped almost all his coin

indicators.note: a lover who has been dropped is a former one, an ex
almost all of a word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a dropped lover is an ex
a bit is a coin, as the old British threepenny bit

explanation.surface: Courtroom evidence that a jilted lover lost nearly all his money.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a court case, which suits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibit is an item of evidence produced in court.

clue.text: Knee joint repaired itself

indicators.note: a repair puts the parts together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A knee joint that healed on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: Stifle is not the verb here: it is a horse's knee joint, on the hind leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The stifle is the joint in a horse's hind leg corresponding to the human knee.

clue.text: Phone-in with Old English confused naive character

indicators.note: confused means jumbled together, so the letters lose their order

explanation.surface: A radio phone-in caller baffled by Anglo-Saxon is a simple soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie-the-Pooh, A. A. Milne's bear 'of very little brain', is a naive character.

clue.text: Gold and silver backing on new church keys

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so AG turns round
in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Donors of gold and silver backing a new church's keys.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the silver turns round; OR stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ is the church's keyboard instrument, so it is its keys.

clue.text: Drop American following Live Aid’s conclusion

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the American comes after the verb
a word's conclusion is its last letter

blocks.note: to be is to live, exist

explanation.surface: An American giving up after the end of the Live Aid concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Live Aid was the 1985 charity concert, and the capitals hide that 'Live' means exist.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bead of sweat or dew is a small rounded drop.

clue.text: Up to nothing Scots fall back

indicators.note: back turns the whole assembly round

explanation.surface: A Scot scheming to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up to nothing' reads as a phrase meaning idle; 'Up' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: afoot means astir, up and about, the way people are up early.

clue.text: Delicate female called bachelor in French island

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, so the bachelor sits within the island

explanation.surface: A fragile woman phoned a single man on an island off France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delicate female' looks like one phrase; the definition stops at 'Delicate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from the Latin frangere, to break: easily broken.

clue.text: Very good shot paralysed investigator

blocks.note: a dead limb is numb, paralysed
a private eye is an investigator

explanation.surface: A crack marksman leaves a detective unable to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' pretends to be the investigator's wound; it is the marksman.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from American slang: a marksman who never misses.

clue.text: Saw nurses at work made contribution

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so DATED holds ON

blocks.note: to see someone is to date them

explanation.surface: Seeing the nurses at their job moved someone to give.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a noun or the tool; it is the verb, as in seeing someone romantically. 'Nurses' is the containment verb, not hospital staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: to give money or goods to a cause.
